title: Yellow Banana Squash Crème Brûlée
notes: Coconut Butter. Coconut Butter is different from coconut oil. It is simply dried coconut flesh that has been broken down in a food processor or blender until it is buttery in texture. It is easy enough to make at home with a bit of patience and a lot of scraping down to sides of a processor but can also be store bought. See note about Coconut Nectar on page 114. Psyllium Husk. Psyllium husk is a natural dietary fibre that is great for mild digestion problems (in higher doses than this recipe uses). It also acts as a binding agent to help set dishes, especially desserts, that aren’t cooked. Gluten-free, diabetic friendly, nut free.

ingredientSections.heading: Crème Brûlée
items: 360g baked banana squash or butternut squash

ingredientSections.heading: Garnish
items: ½ Cup brown sugar for glaze (optional)

methodSections.heading: Crème Brûlée
steps: Cut the squash in half lengthwise and scoop out the seeds. Bake at 190°C (375°F), cut-side-down on baking tray for 30 minutes or until soft. When cooked, remove the squash skin and cube the flesh.

Remove the vanilla seeds from the pod and discard the pod. Combine 360g of the baked squash along with all the remaining ingredients, except the optional brown sugar, in a high speed blender and blend until completely smooth.
Spoon the blended mixture into oven-safe ramekins or small dishes and smooth out the tops neatly.

methodSections.heading: Garnish
steps: Before serving, if desired, sprinkle about 1 tsp of brown sugar evenly over each dish and use a blow torch to brown and melt the sugar.

If you don’t have a blow torch, simply place the dishes on the top rack of the oven closest to the broiler. With the oven set to a high broil watch very carefully and rotate as needed so each dish browns evenly.
Top with a sprig of mint and a physalis or your choice of garnish.
